regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Recovery and Distribution of Surplus Food) Regulations, 2019
clause: Regulation 3 - Responsibilities of Food Business Operators
title: General Responsibilities of Donors and Waste Disposers
text: Any Food Business Operator (FBO) initiating surplus food recovery or commercial disposal must be registered or licensed under FSSAI. FBOs must segregate food fit for consumption from spoiled or unwholesome food at source. Clear records must be maintained indicating the date of collection, nature of food, quantity, and the certified recipient or disposal facility.
legal_mandate: Mandatory record-keeping and source segregation for all licensed food businesses.
tier_rule: Businesses must be verified with active FSSAI registration before pickups are permitted.

regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Recovery and Distribution of Surplus Food) Regulations, 2019
clause: Regulation 4 - Safe Handling and Temperature Maintenance
title: Temperature Control and Time Limits for Perishables
text: Hot cooked surplus food must be maintained at or above 65°C until delivery. Cold perishable food (dairy, cut fruits) must be kept below 5°C. Unchilled cooked food held at ambient room temperature must be consumed within a maximum window of 4 hours from preparation. Once the 4-hour window lapses, human consumption is strictly prohibited due to microbial growth risk.
legal_mandate: Perishable food past the safe temperature holding window cannot enter human processing.
tier_rule: Cooked food exceeding safe holding limits is strictly locked out of Tiers B and C, routing exclusively to Tier D (Biogas/Compost).

regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Recovery and Distribution of Surplus Food) Regulations, 2019
clause: Regulation 5 - Food Not Fit for Human Consumption
title: Strict Lockout of Expired, Damaged, and Spoiled Stock
text: Food that has crossed its expiry date, use-by date, or displays observable spoilage (mold growth, fermentation, unpleasant odor, insect infestation, or slime) is legally defined as unfit for human consumption. It is prohibited to sell, donate, process, or redirect expired stock into food manufacturing.
legal_mandate: Immediate mandatory lock-out of expired stock from all human food and edible processing chains.
tier_rule: Expired or spoiled lots are automatically locked out of Tiers B (Process) and C (Feed). Allowed destination is strictly Tier D (Certified Compost / Anaerobic Digestion).

regulation: Livestock Feed and Swill Feeding Prevention Guidelines
clause: Section 4 - Prohibited Materials in Animal Feed
title: Animal Feed Safety and Swill Feeding Restrictions
text: To prevent Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) and zoonotic pathogens, feeding catering waste, meat scraps, or poultry-contaminated swill to cattle, sheep, goats, and livestock is strictly illegal. Animal feed manufacturers may only accept clean, unexpired, vegetarian surplus such as bakery scraps, non-moldy grain residues, and clean fruit/vegetable trimmings. Expired, moldy, or mycotoxin-contaminated grains are strictly banned from feed.
legal_mandate: Non-vegetarian catering waste, expired foods, and moldy produce must never be routed to livestock feed.
tier_rule: Tier C (Feed) is permitted ONLY for non-expired, vegetarian bakery, grain, fruit, and vegetable surplus. Expired items, meat, and dairy waste are locked out of Tier C.

regulation: Advisory on Safe Utilization of Vegetarian Catering Surplus for Livestock
clause: Clause 4.2 - Cereal, Bakery, and Roti Donation to Bovine Shelters (Gaushalas)
title: Donation of Bread, Roti, and Grain Residues to Gaushalas and Cattle Shelters
text: Clean, mold-free, unexpired vegetarian cereal products—including dry rotis, chapatis, bread surplus, unfermented boiled grains, and clean vegetable peels—are legally PERMITTED to be supplied to registered Gaushalas (cattle shelters) and livestock feed mills under Tier C. However, rotis showing any signs of fungal mold (Rhizopus or Aspergillus producing aflatoxins), wet rotis stored in humid containers exceeding 24 hours, or rotis mixed with spicy/oily cooked curries, dal, or non-vegetarian catering swill are strictly prohibited from animal feed due to severe rumen acidosis and mycotoxin risks. Moldy or spoiled rotis must be diverted to Tier D (compost/biogas).
legal_mandate: Clean, vegetarian, mold-free rotis and bakery surplus can be fed to cows/gaushalas; moldy or oily cooked waste is strictly banned.
tier_rule: FoodLoop approves clean dry rotis/chapatis for Tier C (Gaushala / Cattle Feed); flags moldy or curry-soaked stock for Tier D (Biogas / Compost).

authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) & CPCB
title: Source Segregation of Biodegradable Organic Waste
text: All commercial establishments, restaurants, and hotels producing biodegradable organic waste must segregate waste at source into distinct streams (biodegradable, non-biodegradable recyclable, and domestic hazardous). Mixing spoiled food waste with plastics, metals, or hazardous chemicals is prohibited. Bulk waste generators must ensure organic waste is directed to bio-methanation or licensed composting units rather than municipal landfills.
legal_mandate: Zero mixing of biodegradable organic waste with packaging or hazardous trash.
tier_rule: FoodLoop enforces packaging segregation (Tier E) and certified industrial composting/biogas processing (Tier D) for bulk organic streams.

regulation: Criteria for Certified Composting and Anaerobic Digestion Facilities
clause: Schedule II - Standards for Processing Facilities
title: Certification Standards for Compost and Biogas Units
text: Composting and anaerobic digestion facilities receiving commercial organic food waste must possess valid State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) Consent to Operate (CTO). Facilities must meet leachate control, odor abatement, and temperature pathogen-reduction thresholds (minimum 55°C for 3 consecutive days during composting). Untreated open dumping of food waste is an environmental violation.
legal_mandate: Disposal facilities must hold verified SPCB/CPCB environmental compliance certificates.
tier_rule: FoodLoop requires platform admin validation of destination facility certificates before routing Tier D waste.

title: Statutory Penalties for Willful Distribution of Unsafe Food
text: Any person or enterprise that manufactures, stores, sells, distributes, or imports unsafe food—whether for human consumption or human-derived food products—faces criminal penalties. If such distribution does not cause injury, punishment includes fine up to ₹1,00,000; non-grievous injury incurs imprisonment up to 1 year and fine up to ₹3,00,000; grievous injury or fatality incurs imprisonment from 7 years to life imprisonment and minimum fine of ₹10,00,000.
legal_mandate: Strict enterprise liability for distributing spoiled or expired stock for consumption.
tier_rule: FoodLoop's hardcoded tier locks protect businesses by physically preventing expired/spoiled lots from being routed to human or livestock processors.

regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Recovery and Distribution of Surplus Food) Regulations, 2019
title: Audit Trail and Tamper-Evident Transport Requirements
text: Surplus and disposed food consignments must be traceable throughout their journey from source to destination. Consignments must be identified with batch details, dispatch timestamp, designated disposal route, and receiving facility. Tamper-evident transit documentation must be generated to verify that waste was delivered to certified recovery centers without unauthorized en-route diversion.
legal_mandate: Traceability and verifiable delivery documentation required for commercial food waste dispatch.
tier_rule: FoodLoop's SHA-256 hash-chained disposal records (FL-YYYY-XXXXX) fulfill Regulation 6's statutory requirement for verifiable, tamper-evident audit trails.

regulation: Repurpose Used Cooking Oil (RUCO) Guidelines & Regulation
clause: Direction under Section 16(5) - Disposal of Used Cooking Oil
title: Mandatory Collection and Biodiesel Conversion of Used Cooking Oil
text: Cooking oil with Total Polar Compounds (TPC) exceeding 25% is classified as hazardous to cardiovascular health and strictly illegal to reuse or blend back into human food chains. Any Food Business Operator consuming more than 50 litres of edible oil per day must maintain an oil purchase/disposal logbook and hand over used oil exclusively to FSSAI-authorized biodiesel aggregators. Discharging used cooking oil into municipal drains or open land is strictly prohibited.
legal_mandate: Degraded cooking oil (TPC > 25%) cannot be reused for food or poured into sewage; must be routed to certified biofuel processors.
tier_rule: FoodLoop routes used fryer and cooking oil exclusively to certified Tier E (Industrial Recycling / Biodiesel).

authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
clause: Rule 9 - Prescribed Standards for De-packaging and Segregation
title: Mandatory De-packaging of Spoiled and Packaged Food Waste
text: Commercial food waste packaged in multi-layered plastics, sachets, polybags, or aluminum foils must be systematically de-packaged prior to loading into composting heaps or anaerobic digestion digesters. Non-biodegradable plastics introduce microplastic contamination into agricultural compost, rendering the organic fertilizer non-compliant with FCO (Fertilizer Control Order) standards.
legal_mandate: Zero plastic packaging contamination in organic compost or anaerobic biogas digesters.
tier_rule: FoodLoop flags packaged lots for mandatory manual or mechanical de-packaging, routing clean packaging to Tier E (Recycling).

regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Schedule IV
clause: Schedule IV - Specific Sanitary Practices for Cold Chain Logistics
title: Cold Chain Integrity and Temperature Breach Protocol
text: Chilled food items (dairy, butchery meats, vaccine-sensitive biologicals) must be transported in temperature-controlled reefer vehicles maintaining core temperatures below 5°C continuously. If a temperature breach exceeding 8°C persists for more than 2 hours during transit, the consignment is considered temperature-abused and compromised. Such stock is forbidden from human retail or charitable donation.
legal_mandate: Temperature-abused chilled items cannot enter human consumption after a transit cold chain failure.
tier_rule: Lots suffering cold chain failure are locked out of Tiers B and C, diverted directly to Tier D (Biogas / Composting).

clause: Rule 3(1)(7) & Rule 4(7) - Bulk Waste Generator On-Site Mandate
title: Bulk Waste Generator On-Site Composting and Landfill Ban
text: Any establishment, commercial complex, hotel, banquet hall, or catering business generating an average of more than 100 kg of waste per day across all streams is classified as a Bulk Waste Generator (BWG). BWGs are legally prohibited from handing unsegregated organic waste to municipal collection vehicles for landfilling. BWGs must process wet waste on-site via biomethanation/composting or engage an authorized off-site recovery network.
legal_mandate: Establishments producing >100 kg/day of waste cannot dump organic waste in landfills.
tier_rule: FoodLoop provides verified digital consignment dispatch proof so BWGs can demonstrate 100% landfill diversion compliance to municipal inspectors.
